question: Freezing European funding to Libya following the ratification of the TurkishLibyan Memorandum

On 20 October 2026, Libya’s House of Representatives ratified the 2019 Türkiye-Libya Memorandum of Understanding on the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions, which ignores the maritime rights of Greek islands.

The Presidents of the European Commission and the European Council declared it ‘null and void’, contrary to the Law of the Sea and in breach of the sovereign rights of third states, reaffirming their solidarity with Greece and Cyprus1. Meanwhile, arrivals of migrants in Crete and Gavdos increased from 4 935 in 2024 to 19 799 in 2025 and in 2026, as many as 8 552 arrivals were recorded in the first half of the year.

Of those who arrived in 2025, 99.4 % had departed from Libya234. The EU has earmarked EUR 224 million for Libya for the period 2021-20275 and an additional EUR 25 million in funding on migration cooperation6. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What amounts has it approved, committed and disbursed to Libya since 2021, by programme, year and final recipient, to the authorities of eastern Libya?

Will it consider suspending all European funding to Libya, including the sum of EUR 25 million, until the Memorandum is repealed, providing justifications for any exemptions on humanitarian or legal grounds?
Will it propose to the Council the suspension of political cooperation and the consideration of restrictive measures until the ratification is revoked?
